item.research_question: Whether the ordered oxygen complex (OOC) strengthening mechanism, previously observed in high-entropy alloys, can be extended to medium-entropy alloys and how the formation of OOCs can be tailored by adjusting alloy composition.
item.material_system: Ti–30Zr–xNb–yO medium-entropy alloys (x = 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30 at.% Nb; y = 0, 1, 2, 3, 3.5, 4 at.% O)
item.processing_route: Arc-melting of pure metals and TiO2 in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere, followed by remelting at least six times and drop-casting into a water-cooled copper mold (10 × 10 × 60 mm³).
item.test_conditions: Room-temperature tensile tests at a strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; internal-friction measurements at 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 4 Hz with a heating rate of 2 K min⁻¹ from 300 to 1100 K.
key_findings: The tensile yield strength of the Ti-30Zr-14Nb-3O MEA was enhanced by ~75% compared to the base alloy.
The elongation of the Ti-30Zr-14Nb-3O MEA was improved by ~164%, reaching ~25.1% compared to ~9.5% for the base alloy.
The number density of OOCs in Ti-30Zr-14Nb-3O was 8.7 × 10²⁴ m⁻³, significantly higher than the 6.7 × 10²³ m⁻³ found in Ti-30Zr-26Nb-3O.
Decreasing the Nb content from 30 at.% to 14 at.% increased the degree of (Ti, Zr)-rich chemical short-range orderings (CSROs).
The percentage of oxygen atoms involved in OOC formation decreased from ~40.9% in Ti-30Zr-14Nb-3O to ~24.0% in Ti-30Zr-30Nb-3O.
Oxygen content exceeding 3.0 at.% (e.g., 4 at.%) caused grain boundary segregation and a transition to intergranular brittle fracture.
The deformation mode shifted from planar slip to wavy slip as the number density of OOCs increased with oxygen doping.
item.mechanism: Decreasing phase stability (by reducing Nb content) enhances (Ti, Zr)-rich CSROs, which act as preferential sites for oxygen to occupy octahedral interstitial positions, forming OOCs. These OOCs provide interstitial solid-solution hardening to increase strength and act as dislocation pinning centers that promote cross-slip and wavy slip, thereby enhancing ductility. Excessive oxygen leads to grain boundary segregation, causing embrittlement.
item.limitations: The ductility dramatically deteriorates with oxygen concentration in the Ti–30Zr–10Nb MEA due to the suppression of martensite phase transformation or twin formation. Excessive oxygen addition (>3.0 at.%) causes grain boundary segregation and brittle fracture.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the strategy of creating OOCs via promoting (Ti, Zr)-enriched CSROs can be extended to Zr-based and Ti-based conventional alloys, as well as Zr–Ti–Nb–M (M = other metals) high-entropy alloys.
quotes: Ordered oxygen complexes (OOCs), a state between random interstitials and oxides, can simultaneously enhance strength and ductility in high-entropy alloys.
The tensile yield strength is enhanced by ~75% and ductility is substantially improved by ~164% with addition of 3.0 at.% O in the Ti-30Zr-14Nb MEA.
